description: MXFP4 GEMM: (a * a_scale) @ (b * b_scale).T, e2m1 values packed two per byte, one e8m0 scale per 1 x 32. aiter gemm_a4w4 (asm / CK / FlyDSL), MXFP4 checkpoints (GLM-5.x MXFP4, Kimi).

layout.doc: b_shuffled: b preshuffled 16x16 and both scales from dynamic_mxfp4_quant(shuffle=True)

hooks.mxfp4_quant: (name, spec, shape, dtype, sym, gen, device) -> {name: (packed, logical), spec.dist.scale_input: (scales, logical_scales)}. Draw the float source from dist.source with `gen`, quantize it with the INSTALLED quantizer (aiter dynamic_mxfp4_quant, shuffle per the layout attr), and return as logical the float64 dequantization of the UNshuffled packed values and scales (reference_f64.dequant_mxfp4 / decode_e8m0). Never pack fp4 by hand.

call: Pass packed a/b and their e8m0 scales as the live caller does (shuffled when layout == 'b_shuffled'); return out.

timing.cache: b/b_scale are weights; a/a_scale are produced by the preceding fused quant kernel and are L2-warm in serving.

negative_controls: use scale block j+1 for block j on the last K block
flip the nibble order of one packed operand load (low/high): a large, unbiased error the bound rejects
pitfalls: Packed bytes are not numbers: compare the GEMM output, and if a quantized intermediate is ever an output, compare it bytes_exact (rel error over packed bytes means nothing).
The quantizer is part of the input contract: a hand-written e2m1 packer that disagrees with dynamic_mxfp4_quant on rounding or nibble order produces a valid-looking but different operand.
Scale padding: aiter pads e8m0 scales to (256, 8) when shuffling; inside the domain (k % 256 == 0) the padding is a no-op, outside it the shuffled scale shape differs from (m, k/32).
kernelName ending in _fp4 in a fused-MoE CSV means the activation quant is fused in; that is a different operator boundary from this GEMM.
